To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a simple and sensitive procedure was developed for the first time for the determination of the five terpenes in the leaves of N. langdorffii and that the method was applied to in vivo and in vitro wild-type (wt) and transgenic specimens subjected to chemical and heat stress.

a simple and sensitive headspace solid-phase extraction method followed by gas-chromatography with mass spectrometer analysis was developed for the analysis of five terpenoid compounds in Nicotiana Langsdorffii, which is a plant species that is used as a model to study abiotic stress in plants.

the proposed headspace solid-phase-microextraction method followed GC/MS is suitable for determining terpene levels in the leaves of N. langdsorffii and can be used for the analysis of other plant species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the analysis of terpenes, which could be applied to other plant species.
the development of a simple, rapid, sensitive, and reproducible method for the determination of volatile terpenes in N. langsdorfii leaves.

the optimization of a simple, sensitive and reliable method to determine the terpene profile of Nicotiana plants, and with the application of the method to the analysis of wild-type and transgenics subjected to abiotic stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed method is suitable for the determination of low concentration levels of five terpenoid compounds in plant tissues.

the optimized method is suitable for the determination of the five terpenes in N. langsdoffii, but the low concentration levels found in the samples suggest the need for an alternative extraction procedure.

the proposed analytical method can be used for the determination of the selected terpenes in the leaves of N. langsfodffii, but it is also suitable for the analysis of terpene content variations induced by abiotic stresses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimized headspace solid-phase extraction method followed by GC-MS is a suitable and sensitive tool for the determination of the terpenes α-pinene, limone, linalool and α-terpineo in Nicotiana leaves.
the proposed method is suitable for the determination of trace levels of terpenic compounds, and it can be applied to the analysis of plant extracts.
the developed method is a good compromise between the analytical requirements of sensitivity, repeatability, and speed, and the need for a low cost and easy-to-use procedure.

HS-SPME is an effective and simple method for the determination of low concentration levels of volatile organic compounds in plant material.
the developed procedure can be used to determine terpenes in plants and to investigate their role as stress biomarkers.
